question: Which providers hand out a free or anonymous Linux VM or shell that answers SSH, and what does each one cost, last for, and require?

host.egress: an HTTP CONNECT proxy at 169.254.169.1 that permits 443 and refuses port 22 with HTTP 403
host.note: Two consequences, both measured and both load-bearing. (1) No provider's port 22 can be reached directly from this sandbox, so every reachability claim below was checked through the tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev forward path, using that relay's own /trace diagnostic. (2) The relay's forward path carries an SSH banner and then stops, so 'the relay can reach it' is a statement about a banner, NOT about a completed login. See research/verification/ssh-relay-2026-10-02.md.

classes.anonymous: No account and no card. The provider identifies the machine by the SSH key that created it.
classes.free-account: A free account is required. No card is charged for the free quota, but signup is mandatory.
classes.free-tier-card: A card is required at signup. A recurring or time-boxed free allowance covers the machine.
classes.changed: The offer this list used to cite is gone or has changed. Recorded so citing it as live is a mistake this page prevents.

ssh_reachability_legend.banner-verified: The relay dialed the host and read its SSH banner (its version string). This proves the host is up and speaking SSH. It does NOT prove a login completes: the relay's forward path stops before KEX_ECDH_REPLY on every target tested, including this one.
ssh_reachability_legend.not-verified: The host could not be dialled from the relay, or the provider publishes no SSH endpoint. Carries the reason.
ssh_reachability_legend.provider-documented: The provider's own page publishes the SSH path. Not independently dialled from this host.

rows.name: Railway Free VM
rows.ssh_how: ssh railway.new, with any ed25519 key as the identity
rows.resources: 2 vCPU / 2 GB, coding agents preinstalled (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Grok, pi, Railway Agent); a shared $3 AI budget per box
rows.lifetime: 60-minute build window, then 24 h to claim; unclaimed boxes and their files are deleted
rows.quote: No. Railway identifies you by your SSH key. If you don't have one, run ssh-keygen -t ed25519 and connect again. You only sign up if you want to keep the box.
rows.verification: first-party-fetched 2026-10-02 (162,813 bytes, HTTP 200); relay /trace dialed railway.new:22 and read banner SSH-2.0-Go
rows.caveats: The ONLY row here that needs no account at all. Anonymous trials are capped per region and can be disabled under demand (the page's own words: "Anonymous trials are temporarily disabled"); the preview URL is visible only from the creating IP until claimed; abuse protections and a shared AI budget apply. Reaching it FROM THIS SANDBOX over the relay gets as far as the SSH banner and then the relay link closes before key exchange completes, so a working login here is not established. See research/verification/ssh-relay-2026-10-02.md.

rows.name: SDF Public Access UNIX System
rows.ssh_how: ssh new@sdf.org creates the account, then ssh USER@sdf.org
rows.resources: shared multi-user UNIX host, not a private VM
rows.lifetime: free USER tier for as long as the account is used
rows.quote: Signup for Shell Access ... [UNIX SHELL] ... Est. 1987
rows.verification: first-party-fetched 2026-10-02 (HTTP 200); relay /trace dialed sdf.org:22 and read banner SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_10.4
rows.caveats: A shared shell, not a VM. The same site is reachable at freeshell.org and webstats.freeshell.org, which both resolve to this one system rather than being three providers.

rows.name: tilde.guru
rows.ssh_how: SSH; the site is a FreeBSD pubnix
rows.resources: FreeBSD pubnix, member of the tildeverse; every user's home is served as a public web page
rows.lifetime: free while active
rows.quote: a FreeBSD pubnix · est. 2021 · member of the tildeverse ... SYSTEM ONLINE — FreeBSD 15.0-RELEASE
rows.verification: first-party-fetched 2026-10-02 (HTTP 200); relay /trace dialed tilde.guru:22 and read banner SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_10.0 FreeBSD-20250801
rows.caveats: NEW ROW, not in the earlier census. FreeBSD, not Linux. Shared shell, not a VM. Signup and resource limits are on the site's own wiki, which returned 404 for /wiki/Join when fetched here.

rows.lifetime: free while active
rows.quote: SSH fingerprints: SHA256:M2URWy/QGPdn8K1XHA5KEWQs+7RtqKCkHCqp1NyxFyI (RSA)
rows.verification: first-party-fetched 2026-10-02; relay /trace dialed tilde.club:22 and read banner SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_10.0

rows.name: tilde.town
rows.ssh_how: SSH; the site publishes the host ECDSA key
rows.resources: shared shell account
rows.lifetime: free while active
rows.quote: ecdsa host key: SHA256:RNFVaXxh2wnrolcByZQBRxRZDFBb2HRCnNq/g9ZGRp0
rows.verification: first-party-fetched 2026-10-02; relay /trace dialed tilde.town:22 and read banner SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_10.0p2 Debian-7+deb13u4

rows.name: tilde.zone
rows.ssh_how: SSH; member of the tildeverse
rows.resources: shared shell account
rows.lifetime: free while active
rows.verification: reachability measured 2026-10-02: relay /trace dialed tilde.zone:22 and read banner SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_10.0p2 Debian-7+deb13u4
rows.caveats: NEW ROW and the WEAKEST evidence in this census: the host was dialled and answered with an OpenSSH banner, and nothing else about it was checked first-party. Same Debian build string as tilde.town, which is what a shared image or a mirror would produce; that is a reason to verify the operator before relying on it, not a claim that they are the same host. No signup page was fetched.

rows.name: hashbang (#!)
rows.ssh_how: POST your public key to https://hashbang.sh/user/create with a username and host, then ssh username@host
rows.resources: shared shell server; the project's stats endpoint advertises maxusers 6175
rows.lifetime: free shell account, community-run
rows.quote: curl -d '{"user":"someuser","key":"'"$(cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub)"'","host":"someHost.hashbang.sh"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' https://hashbang.sh/user/create
rows.verification: first-party-fetched 2026-10-02; the node was named by hashbang's OWN https://hashbang.sh/server/stats API (de1.hashbang.sh) and the relay dialled de1.hashbang.sh:22, reading banner SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.2p1 Debian-2+deb12u10
rows.caveats: CORRECTION to an earlier census: the host in the documented example, someHost.hashbang.sh, does not resolve (the relay: "no A/AAAA records"). The real node name comes from hashbang's own /server/stats. Account creation needs no account and no card - a public key IS the account - which makes it the closest thing to anonymous here besides Railway, but it is not classified anonymous because the operator reserves the right to refuse and the account has a human owner.

rows.name: Blinkenshell
rows.ssh_how: SSH on the NON-STANDARD port 2222, which the project's own FAQ states
rows.resources: shared UNIX shell provider, online continuously since 2006
rows.lifetime: free account; new members accepted
rows.quote: Blinkenshell uses the non-standard port 2222 for SSH (instead of 22), so you need to specify this when connecting.
rows.verification: first-party-fetched 2026-10-02 (HTTP 200); its wiki/FAQ carries the port-2222 sentence quoted above
rows.caveats: NEW ROW. NOT reachable from here and the reason is measured, not assumed: the relay dialed blinkenshell.org on 22, 2222 and 443 and every one answered silent-or-unreachable at 0 bytes, so the host is refusing or filtering this network rather than being down. Signup is a multi-step process that ends in a VOUCH by an existing member, and the FAQ states you cannot SSH until you reach step 5. It is a shared shell, not a VM. The port-2222 fact is the useful part: a scanner that only tries 22 records every Blinkenshell-class host as dead.

rows.name: GitHub Codespaces
rows.ssh_how: gh codespace ssh -c CODESPACE-NAME; the default dev container runs an SSH server
rows.resources: 2-core default machine; choose 2/4/8/16/32-core
rows.lifetime: quota resets monthly; a codespace is deleted after its retention period of inactivity
rows.quote: GitHub will provide users in the free plan 120 core hours or 60 hours of run time on a 2 core codespace, plus 15 GB of storage each month.
rows.verification: provider-documented; no published host:port to dial, so nothing was checked from this host
rows.caveats: Free quota is for personal accounts only; organizations and enterprises must pay. Storage beyond 15 GB-month and compute beyond the quota are billed.

rows.name: Google Cloud Shell
rows.ssh_how: Open in the browser or connect with the gcloud CLI
rows.ssh_endpoint: published per-session by Google Cloud Shell
rows.resources: temporary Compute Engine VM, 5 GB persistent $HOME
rows.lifetime: ephemeral VM per session; the 5 GB $HOME persists
rows.quote: The default weekly Cloud Shell quota is 50 hours.
rows.caveats: Sign-in with a Google account is required. Exceeding the weekly quota suspends Cloud Shell until the next week. The VM is recreated, so only $HOME survives.

rows.name: alwaysdata Free
rows.ssh_how: SSH to the account's user; alwaysdata documents SSH users, keys and 2FA
rows.resources: 1 GB SSD, 256 MB RAM, 1/4 CPU, shared hosting
rows.lifetime: the free offer is described as available for life
rows.quote: Free ... 0 €/month ... Disk space SSD 1 Go gift RAM 256 Mo free CPU 1/4 ... for life
rows.verification: first-party-fetched 2026-10-02; the relay dialed alwaysdata.com:22 and read 0 bytes, but that host is a shared web front end and the account's SSH host is per-account, so this is not evidence about the service
rows.caveats: Shared web-hosting account, not a root VM; the free quota is small and some services are restricted.

rows.name: Oracle Cloud Always Free
rows.ssh_how: SSH key is installed at instance creation; the console and the CLI both connect
rows.ssh_endpoint: per-instance, public IP assigned by Oracle
rows.resources: 2 AMD micro VMs and up to 4 OCPU / 24 GB Arm Ampere A1 across one or more instances; 200 GB block storage
rows.lifetime: Always Free, no time limit, while the tenancy qualifies
rows.quote: All tenancies get the first 1,500 OCPU hours and 9,000 GB hours per month for free for VM instances using the VM.Standard.A1.Flex shape (carried from research/verification/2026-10-02.md; the oracle.com domain returns 403 to this host)
rows.verification: blocked-from-host: every oracle.com URL returns a 1,339-byte export-control 403 here; the corpus card and the quoted allowance are the evidence
rows.caveats: A card is required at signup and capacity can be reclaimed; A1 is often out of capacity in a region. The allowance is a resource allowance, not a dollar credit.

rows.name: Google Cloud Free Tier (e2-micro)
rows.ssh_how: SSH keys are added to the instance or its project metadata
rows.ssh_endpoint: per-instance, external IP assigned by Google
rows.resources: 1 non-preemptible e2-micro, 30 GB standard persistent disk, 1 GB egress
rows.lifetime: every month, for the life of the account
rows.quote: 1 non-preemptible e2-micro VM instance per month in one of the following US regions ... 30 GB-months standard persistent disk ... 1 GB of outbound data transfer ... per month.
rows.caveats: A billing account with a card is required. The allowance is one e2-micro in us-west1, us-central1 or us-east1; the $300 signup credit is one-time and separate.

rows.name: AWS Free Tier
rows.ssh_how: SSH key pair is chosen at instance launch
rows.ssh_endpoint: per-instance, public IP assigned by AWS
rows.resources: EC2 instances up to the plan's credit; the current free plan is credit-based (up to $200 over 6 months)
rows.lifetime: 6 months, or until the credits run out; the account then closes on its own unless converted to paid
rows.quote: When you create a new AWS Free Tier account, you get $100 in credits immediately. As you explore key services, you can earn up to $100 more. That's up to $200 over 6 months ... The account closes on its own 6 months after you open it or when your credits run out, whichever comes first.
rows.caveats: A card is required. The free plan is time-boxed and closes itself; the old 750-hours-for-12-months t2.micro offer is no longer the headline shape of the plan.

rows.name: Azure Free Account
rows.ssh_how: SSH keys are set at VM creation; the portal and the CLI both connect
rows.ssh_endpoint: per-instance, public IP assigned by Azure
rows.resources: 750 hours each of B1s, B2pts v2 (Arm) and B2ats v2 (AMD) burstable VMs, plus 65+ always-free services
rows.lifetime: the VM hours are 12 months for new customers; the $200 credit lasts 30 days; always-free services do not expire
rows.quote: 12 months Azure Virtual Machines for Linux or Windows 750 hours each of B1s, B2pts v2 (Arm-based), and B2ats v2 (AMD-based) burstable VMs ... $200 credit to use on Azure services within 30 days
rows.caveats: A card is required and a temporary $1 authorization may be placed at signup. The 750-hour VM allowance is 12 months only; the $200 credit is 30 days.

rows.name: Modal Starter
rows.ssh_how: modal shell into a sandbox container from the Modal CLI
rows.ssh_endpoint: not published; reached through the Modal CLI
rows.resources: containers and sandboxes on Modal's pool; 1 TiB/month free egress
rows.lifetime: monthly credit reissued each month
rows.quote: $0 + compute / month ... $30 / month free credits ... 1 TiB / month free network egress
rows.caveats: An account is required; the $30 is a monthly credit, not a permanent free machine. It is a container sandbox, not a general VPS.

rows.name: Hugging Face Spaces (CPU)
rows.ssh_how: Spaces Dev Mode exposes an SSH endpoint for a running Space
rows.ssh_endpoint: per-Space, published while the Space runs
rows.resources: free CPU basic Space (2 vCPU / 16 GB)
rows.lifetime: while the Space exists and is built
rows.quote: Spaces Hardware ... Starting at $0.
rows.caveats: A free account is required. It is an app host, not a general VM; Dev Mode is the documented way to get a shell and its availability should be checked against the current docs.

rows.name: Killercoda
rows.ssh_how: browser terminal; no inbound SSH published
rows.resources: Linux or Kubernetes scenario environment
rows.lifetime: FREE scenario runs up to 1 hour; PLUS up to 4 hours and 3 concurrent scenarios
rows.quote: Membership PLUS Includes all from FREE Use scenarios for up to 4 hours instead of just one ... Open up to 3 scenarios at the same time
rows.verification: first-party-fetched 2026-10-02; the relay dialed killercoda.com:22 and read 0 bytes, which is consistent with a browser-only product
rows.caveats: The page does not state whether a login is required to start a free scenario; treat 'anonymous' as unverified. Browser terminal only, no SSH.

rows.name: Northflank Sandbox tier
rows.ssh_how: No published inbound SSH; deploy services and use the web console or API
rows.resources: 2 free services, 1 free database, 2 free cron jobs, always-on
rows.lifetime: free while the account is used
rows.quote: Tiers Sandbox ... Always-on-compute - no sleeping :) 2x free services 1x free database 2x free cron jobs
rows.caveats: A container platform, not a VM you SSH into; the free tier is for testing and building trust.

rows.name: Render Free compute
rows.ssh_how: No published inbound SSH for free web services
rows.resources: 512 MB RAM, less than 1 CPU
rows.lifetime: free compute plans have usage limits and are for exploration and previews
rows.quote: Free ( limitations apply ) $0/month 512 MB RAM free Less than 1 CPU
rows.caveats: Web services, key-value and Postgres - not a VM. Free instances sleep and are not for production.

rows.name: AWS CloudShell
rows.ssh_how: Browser terminal only; no inbound SSH endpoint is published
rows.resources: 1 GB persistent storage per AWS Region
rows.lifetime: session persists within the Region; idle sessions end
rows.quote: Run scripts and commands at no extra cost, with up to 1 GB of persistent storage per AWS Region.
rows.caveats: An AWS account is required. It is a browser shell, not a machine you can SSH into from elsewhere.

rows.name: Azure Cloud Shell
rows.ssh_how: Browser terminal only; no inbound SSH endpoint is published
rows.resources: cloud-hosted shell with a persistent Azure Files share
rows.lifetime: session times out after 20 minutes without interactive activity; files persist
rows.cost_usd: 0 for the machine; storage costs apply
rows.quote: Use of the machine hosting Cloud Shell is free. Cloud Shell requires a storage account to host the mounted Azure Files share. Regular storage costs apply.
rows.caveats: An Azure account and a storage account are required; the storage share is billed normally.

rows.name: Fly.io
rows.ssh_how: fly ssh console reaches a running Machine, but there is no free allowance to run one
rows.resources: shared-CPU Machines; volumes first 10 GB free per month
rows.lifetime: pay-as-you-go
rows.cost_usd: no free VM allowance; the only 'first free' is 10 GB of volume capacity
rows.quote: $0.08/GB per month First 10GB free each month
rows.caveats: The free Machine allowance Fly.io used to grant is gone from the pricing page. A card is required; the 10 GB is storage, not compute.

rows.name: Koyeb
rows.ssh_how: No published inbound SSH; the free plan is not in the published tiers
rows.resources: platform services and workers; included usage is a plan feature
rows.lifetime: included usage reissued monthly on paid plans
rows.cost_usd: 0 only if a free tier is still offered; the published Starter/Pro plans carry included usage
rows.quote: Pro $29 /mo +compute ... Included Usage $10 ... Once you've consumed your included monthly free credit, we start billing you on a pay-per-use basis.
rows.caveats: The old free 'Hobby' instance is not in the tiers shown on 2026-10-02; included usage is a paid-plan feature, so a free VM should not be assumed.

rows.name: Play with Docker
rows.ssh_how: browser terminal, never SSH
rows.resources: 4-hour Docker-in-Docker session (historical)
rows.lifetime: unavailable from 2026-03-01
rows.quote: Deprecation notice: Play with Docker will be unavailable starting March 1, 2026.
rows.caveats: Recorded because it is the canonical 'anonymous free VM' many lists still cite. It is gone; Docker Docs now points at supported labs.

rows.name: Microterm, LinuxOnTab
rows.ssh_how: none: both run a Linux kernel inside the browser via WebAssembly (TinyEMU/RISC-V64 and v86)
rows.ssh_endpoint: none: there is no network path to these at all
rows.resources: Alpine userland in-browser, Microterm claims persistent local storage up to 40 GB; LinuxOnTab ships a real x86 kernel and calls itself 'Free, no signup'
rows.lifetime: runs in the reader's own browser tab
rows.quote: Microterm is a fully functional Alpine Linux virtual machine running directly in any browser tab ... local computation with maximum privacy | Free, no signup
rows.caveats: NEW ROW, and the category is new rather than the entries: these are 'anonymous free Linux' with no account and no card, but the machine is the READER'S OWN, there is no host to SSH to, and nothing runs while the tab is closed. Listing them beside a real remote VM would be a category error, which is why they are here rather than in the SSH table. Microterm is RISC-V64 emulated; LinuxOnTab ships a native WebAssembly x86 kernel.
